title: Taifa of Murcia
capsule: The Taifa of Murcia was one of the successor states that emerged from the collapse of the Umayyad Caliphate of Córdoba after 1009, initially governed by the Banu Tahir family. The taifa controlled the southeastern Iberian coast including Murcia, Cartagena, and Lorca, and it submitted to the Almoravid dynasty around 1091; after the Almoravid collapse it re-emerged as the independent Banu Mardanish state under Muhammad ibn Mardanish (the 'Rey Lobo', r. 1147–1172), who allied with Christian kingdoms against the Almohads. The taifa was finally absorbed by the Almohad Caliphate in 1172 after Ibn Mardanish's death, and the later 1228–1243 taifa of Murcia under Ibn Hud preceded Castilian conquest in 1243.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core urban territories of Murcia, Cartagena, and Lorca are documented in Arabic sources; the fluctuating frontiers with Christian kingdoms and neighboring taifas are approximately reconstructed.
